incidents.summary: On August 7, 2026, severe thunderstorms prompted watches and warnings from the National Weather Service across Delaware, New York (including Hudson Valley, Broome, and Sullivan counties), and surrounding states. Over 40,000 New Jersey residents lost power as storms rolled through, while quarter-sized hail and damaging winds affected multiple counties, and lightning caused a weather delay at Nissan Stadium in Tennessee. A Next Weather Alert was in effect for the Philadelphia region due to the combination of heat and heavy storms.

logs.summary: A series of severe storms swept across multiple US states in late July 2026, producing numerous tornadoes—including at least nine in Ohio, six in Kentucky, and four in New Jersey—and causing flash flooding that resulted in at least two confirmed deaths in West Virginia. Damaging winds, large hail, and isolated tornadoes also threatened parts of Manitoba and northwestern Ontario, while extreme heat and additional severe thunderstorm risks were forecast for the Midwest and Northeast.

Meanwhile, in Wisconsin's Fox Cities, recovery efforts continued a week after storms, with over 8,200 meals served and road closures set.

Power outages were reported in the Midlands, and severe weather also forced the Kansas City Chiefs to practice indoors and prompted strong storm alerts in Wisconsin.

logs.summary: On August 2, 2026, a magnitude 5.9 earthquake struck off the east coast of New Zealand's North Island, according to the German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ). The earthquake was located near the Hicks Bay area, consistent with the reported incident. No additional details about damage or tsunami warnings were provided in the news excerpts.
